reading: A small multi-coloured exemplar (centre colour plus a ring and straight arms) sits outside the large rectangles; at every marker inside a rectangle whose colour equals the exemplar's centre, the exemplar's ring is stamped and its arms are extended as full lines to the rectangle's edges. The exemplar itself is erased.
verb: stamp exemplar and extend its arms

slots.exemplar: the multi-coloured component outside the rectangles (centre, 3x3 ring, arm colour and arm directions)
slots.anchors: single cells inside each rectangle with the exemplar's centre colour
slots.arms: for each arm direction present in the exemplar, a line of the arm colour from the anchor to the rectangle edge in both senses
slots.rest: rectangles kept; exemplar cleared to background

why: every anchor gets the exemplar's ring, and lines of the arm colour run in exactly the exemplar's arm directions to the edge of the containing rectangle

reading: The number n of 8s in the top row selects the colours that occur exactly n times in the coloured row below the separator; above each such column a bar of that colour, n cells tall, rises from the separator.

slots.selected columns: columns of the key row whose colour appears exactly n times in that row
slots.bars: the selected colour, in rows sep-n .. sep-1 of each selected column

why: bars appear exactly at columns whose key colour has frequency n, each n tall, ending just above the 5-separator

reading: The single shape is cropped and placed four times around an empty centre square as a pinwheel: original on the left, then rotated 90 degrees for each of top, right, bottom; output is (2w+h) square.

slots.unit: the shape's bounding box (h x w)
slots.layout: output side 2w+h; unit at rows w..w+h-1, cols 0..w-1; the other three copies are its 90/180/270-degree rotations about the output centre

why: the output is invariant under 90-degree rotation and its left arm equals the cropped input shape

reading: Two full horizontal and two full vertical 8-lines cut the grid into a 3x3 panel layout; the four edge-middle panels and the centre are filled by position (top 2, left 4, centre 6, right 3, bottom 1), corners stay empty.

slots.panels: the 3x3 cells cut by the separator lines
slots.colour by position: top-middle 2, middle-left 4, centre 6, middle-right 3, bottom-middle 1, corners unchanged (constants learned from training)

why: each of the five non-corner panels is wholly filled with its position's colour; separators and corner panels unchanged

reading: The 3x3 grid shows one of a few fixed shapes in any colour; the output is a 1x1 cell whose colour codes the shape (2x2 block with opposite corner -> 3, plus -> 6, X -> 2, the 440/404/040 shape -> 1).

slots.shape: the binary mask of the non-background cells, colour ignored
slots.code: lookup learned from training: mask -> output colour

why: pairs with the same mask (regardless of colour) give the same output colour

reading: The most frequent colour in the block above the 5-separator is written into the centre cell of the bottom row; everything else unchanged.

slots.colour: most frequent colour among the rows above the separator

why: exactly one cell changes, the bottom-centre, and it takes the majority colour of the top block

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled to a 3x3 arrangement of 3x3 blocks; a block holds a copy of the input exactly where the input cell has the input's most frequent colour, others are empty.
why: every output block is the input or empty, and the copied blocks are the positions of the most common (background) colour

reading: On an empty grid a clockwise square spiral of 3 is drawn from the top-left corner inward, with one-cell gaps between turns.

slots.start: top-left corner, heading right along row 0
slots.path: clockwise inward spiral, walls of 3 separated by one background lane

why: output is the input-size spiral; only size varies

reading: Two cells sit at the two ends of a row; each extends toward the other in its own colour until they meet, and the middle cell becomes 5.

slots.endpoints: the two coloured cells at the left and right border of one row
slots.halves: each endpoint colour fills its half of the row
slots.midpoint: the centre cell of the row becomes 5

why: the row between the endpoints is filled: left half left colour, right half right colour, centre 5

reading: A two-colour shape lies beside a full separator line of 1; a mirror copy of it in its original colours is added on the other side of the line, and the original shape has its two colours swapped.
verb: reflect across separator and swap colours

slots.axis: the full row or column of 1
slots.copy: the shape reflected across the axis, original colours
slots.original: the shape in place with its two colours exchanged

why: the reflected copy's mask equals the original's mask mirrored; colours a<->b differ between the two sides
